key_insight: WC–Co–Cr coating performance depends on powder morphology and spraying method: detonation spraying favors hardness, while HVOF yields a dense, uniform coating with low friction.
engineering_relevance: Matching feedstock and spray process to service demands can improve coating suitability for machine parts exposed to intensive friction and high loads.
method: Compare detonation-sprayed and HVOF WC–Co–Cr coatings.
Examine powder morphology and coating microstructure using SEM and EDS.
Evaluate coating microhardness and tribological behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an average microhardness of 1449 HV for detonation spraying and a friction coefficient of Kt = 0.143 for HVOF.
watch_item: The abstract omits test conditions, variability, and quantitative wear rates, limiting direct translation to service-life predictions.
paper_title: INVESTIGATION OF THE FORMATION OF STRUCTURE AND WEAR-RESISTANT PROPERTIES OF WC–CO–CR COATINGS PRODUCED BY HVOF AND DETONATION SPRAYING
